question: Was moving the capital automatically from pool to pool ever tested in a backtest, when, and what was the verdict?

facts.a: tested on 26.08: the rotation backtest was built and computed that day
facts.b: on the production engine v1.1 even an oracle knowing the next 7 days lost to 100% USDC on both windows
facts.c: threshold rotation was the worst variant of all (-26 to -30%)
facts.d: switching costs ($317 to 1890) outweighed the value of choosing the pool
facts.e: verdict: do not build automatic rotation between ETH/stable pools

reference: Yes, on 26.08: the rotation backtest (backtest/rotation.ts) was built and run by CC-Win the same day. On the production engine v1.1 even an oracle that knew the next 7 days lost to holding 100% USDC on both windows (-23% on 365 days, -8% on 720 days), threshold rotation was the worst variant of all (-26 to -30%), and switching costs ($317 to 1890) outweighed the value of picking the pool, so automatic rotation between ETH/stable pools was not to be built.
notes: Medium. The live selector also proposed ROTATE moves, but never executed them; the question asks about the backtest. Held-out batch 1 (2026-11-26), written by CC-Mac; review file ai/eval/review/heldout-batch-1.md.

question: When was it known for sure that no strategy beat plain HODL, and why was the project continued if it turned out the strategies did not work?

facts.a: 26.08 evening: the abandonment threshold was met (hedged and flat-only families without an edge; v1.1 below its starting $5k on mainnet/Arbitrum; active management cost more than it gave)
facts.b: one result survived: wide passive LP ±50% beat HODL over the full period on 4/4 pools (an allocation product, not an algorithm)
facts.c: the owner chose one final round instead of an immediate freeze, after the literature showed about half of LPs lose to HODL (results consistent with the market)
facts.d: fixed rule: after that round, product or freeze, no further experiments

reference: On the evening of 26.08 the abandonment threshold set that day was formally met: the hedged and flat-only families showed no edge over their benchmarks, rotation was the worst of all, and the production v1.1 ended below its starting $5k on mainnet and Arbitrum, its active management costing more than it gave. The premise is not quite right: a wide passive LP of ±50% ('HODL with yield') beat HODL over the full period on 4 of 4 pools, as an allocation product rather than an algorithm. The project went on because the owner, after a discussion of the literature (about half of LPs lose to HODL, so the results match the market; full range does best, as the ±50% did), chose one final round instead of freezing at once, under a fixed rule: product or freeze after it, no further experiments.
notes: Owner's wording, part 1 of his question 1 (split proposed, he decides). Polish original: 'kiedy bylo wiadomo ze na pewno zadna strategia nie przebila zwyklego HODL, i dlaczego projekt byl dalej kontynuowany jesli okazalo sie ze strategie nie przynosza efektu'. The 27.08 outcome (hybrid FlatWide, capital in) is left out of the reference: it is dev dated-01's fact and its chunks hold dated-01, id-03 and why-08 evidence (tool check). question: Could the simulation of the algorithms have made a calculation error, so that some strategy actually did beat HODL?
reference: The corpus does not prove the simulator right, but it records how its results were checked and which errors were found: the validation itself caught an engine bug (probe swaps through empty ticks faked trend signals and made exit variants show -100%; filtered on 17.08, baselines unaffected, verdict unchanged); the final round was recomputed independently on 8 of 8 walk-forward files and agreed with CC-Win's reports to the hundredth; a nightly report that called FlatOnly 'better than HODL' when it was only 'positive' was corrected against its own numbers; a corrupted first price point in a 720-day cache was flagged. After the volatility measure was corrected, the recalibration series still passed zero gates, and the overall result matches the literature (about half of LPs lose to HODL). One strategy did beat HODL over the full period, the wide passive ±50%, so the claim concerns the active strategies.

question: How was the problem with displaying the correct currency values in the wallet fixed?

facts.a: cause: the old application computed Uniswap v3 math on floating-point numbers instead of integers, with wrong formulas
facts.b: 10.08: decided to rewrite the core instead of repairing the legacy code
facts.c: 10.08: the math ported to bigint (src/utils/v3math.ts), 2925 of 2925 cases bit for bit equal to @uniswap/v3-sdk
facts.d: the app rewritten on it: liquidity through the SDK, 20-25% slippage hack removed; positions computed exactly from sqrtPriceX96, fees by a static collect() call, 'calibrated scaling' and hard-coded positions removed
facts.e: verified 10.08 against app.uniswap.org on the two mainnet positions: amounts, ranges and fees identical; USD totals 0.05-0.3% apart only because of Uniswap's own ETH price feed

reference: The old application computed Uniswap v3 math on floating-point numbers instead of integers, with wrong formulas, so its amounts disagreed with the Uniswap interface; on 10.08 it was decided to rewrite the core rather than repair it. The same day the math was ported to bigint (src/utils/v3math.ts) and checked bit for bit against @uniswap/v3-sdk in 2925 of 2925 cases; liquidity code moved to the SDK and the 20-25% slippage hack was removed; the positions view computes token amounts exactly from sqrtPriceX96 and reads unclaimed fees with a static collect() call, dropping the old 'calibrated scaling' and hard-coded positions. Checked on 10.08 against app.uniswap.org on the owner's two mainnet positions: token amounts, ranges and fees identical, USD totals within 0.05 to 0.3% only because Uniswap prices ETH from its own feed and HOMOS from the pool.
notes: Owner's question 2, his wording. Polish original: 'w jaki sposob zostal naprawiony problem z wyswietlaniem prawidlowych wartosci walut na portfelu?'. The owner chose the position-values reading (not the token-balance rounding in the open-position window) and asked that the reference cover the cause and the fix; it replaces CC-Mac's ho-why-01 on the same finding (withdrawn in this batch). Held-out batch 2 (2026-11-26), written by owner; review file ai/eval/review/heldout-batch-2.md.
